text: Over the last few years, in working with CityPlace residents and community stakeholders, we have identified a number of street safety concerns and have been working to implement improvements. One such improvement, which was approved by City Council in July 2018 (TE34.210), is to create a new pedestrian crossing at Spadina Avenue on the south side of the existing signalized intersection with Bremner Boulevard and Fort York Boulevard. The Spadina Avenue/ Bremner Boulevard/ Fort York Boulevard intersection is a very busy intersection with many pedestrians, cyclists and vehicles. Currently, pedestrians looking to cross the eight lanes of traffic and two designated TTC streetcar tracks would have to do so only on the north side of Spadina Avenue. City Council on December 17 and 18, 2019, adopted the following: 1. City Council rescind the existing southerly westbound double left-turn lane designation in effect at all times on Bremner Boulevard, between Spadina Avenue and a point 30.5 metres east. 2. City Council designate the southerly westbound lane on Bremner Boulevard, between Spadina Avenue and a point 30.5 metres east, for westbound left turns at all times. 3. City Council prohibit westbound left turns from 3:30 p.m. to 6:30 p.m., Monday to Friday, at the intersection of Front Street West and Blue Jays Way, Toronto Transit Commission vehicles and bicycles excepted. 4.
